title: Elder Du Moulin defines by complete faith yet keeps weak faith without full assurance
source_text: CXXV. Quin ipse Petrus Molinaeus pater, in Thesibus illis ubi fidem definit per assensum adhibitum promissionibus Evangelii, quo fidelis non tantum credit eas esse veras, sed etiam ad se peculiariter pertinere, observat tamen se non albo fidelium expungere quotquot hunc fidei gradum nondum sunt assecuti, & fiduciam illam a Deo quidem juberi, sed non dari omnibus fidelibus eodem tempore, vel mensura: & dari fidem infirmam, nec tamen simulatam, quae certa ejusmodi persuasione adhuc destituitur; & quae non propterea definit esse salutaris. Ex quibus patet virum illum celeberrimum, dum fidem definit per assensum quo quis credit promissiones Evangelii, non tantum esse veras, sed etiam ad se peculiariter pertinere; per id significatum velle qualis fides esse debeat, secundum esse suum completum & perfectum, & ita ut nullus actuum, quos producere apta nata est, illi desit: non vero definire quid ad fidei essentiam necessario requiratur, ita ut sine eo consistere non possit; juxta illud quod superius fuit ex Amesio & Perkinsio notatum.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed Peter Du Moulin the father himself, in those theses where he defines faith by the assent given to the Gospel promises whereby the believer not only believes them true but also peculiarly pertaining to himself, nevertheless observes that he does not strike from the roll of the faithful all who have not yet attained this degree of faith, and that that trust is indeed commanded by God, but not given to all believers at the same time or measure: and that weak yet not feigned faith is given which is still destitute of such certain persuasion; and which does not on that account cease to be saving. From which it is plain that that most celebrated man, when he defines faith by the assent by which someone believes the Gospel promises not only true but peculiarly pertaining to himself, means by that what faith ought to be according to its complete and perfect being, so that none of the acts it is apt to produce is lacking to it — not to define what is necessarily required for faith's essence so that without it it cannot consist; according to what was noted above from Ames and Perkins.
pass_b_english: Elder Du Moulin defines faith as assent that Gospel promises are true and mine — yet refuses to expunge from the faithful those who have not reached that degree.
God commands such trust but does not give it to all at the same time or measure; weak unfeigned faith without that persuasion remains saving.
His definition describes faith's complete perfect stature — not the bare essence without which faith cannot exist (as Ames and Perkins noted).

lemmas.gloss: not to strike from the roll of the faithful
according to its complete and perfect being

rejected: full assurance required for any true faith
